title: Standard cast-off
subtitle: The universal bound edge for finishing a piece of knitting.
excerpt: The standard cast-off (UK) or bind-off (US) passes each knitted stitch over the next to produce a firm, finished edge. Every knitter learns it first.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, Series 1 (1886). Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), pp. 50-52.

glossaryTerms.definition: UK term for the row of interlocking stitches that closes the last row of knitting. US equivalent: bind-off. Produced by knitting two stitches, then passing the first over the second and off the needle, and repeating across the row.

content.text: (abbreviated co; US: bind-off, abbreviated bo) closes the final row of knitting by drawing each stitch through the one before it. The resulting edge is a chain of interlocked loops that lies flat, resists unravelling, and is neat enough to be the finished visible edge of a scarf or collar. It is the first finishing technique every knitter learns. Difficulty: beginner.
Your completed piece with stitches on the needle
Knit the first two stitches onto the right needle in the usual way.
Insert the left needle tip into the first stitch on the right needle (the one to the left).
Pass this stitch over the second stitch and off the right needle. One stitch cast off.
Knit one more stitch. Two stitches are again on the right needle.
Repeat steps 2-4 until one stitch remains on the right needle.
Cut the yarn, leaving a 15 cm tail. Draw the tail through the last stitch and pull to fasten off.

Every pattern that does not specify a cast-off method assumes the standard cast-off. It finishes scarves, dishcloths, hat crowns (after the decrease rounds), and the shoulder seams of flat-knitted garments. On a ribbed edge, the standard cast-off tends to be less stretchy than the ribbing beneath; the stretchy lace cast-off or the sewn cast-off give a more elastic finish where the edge needs to stretch.

items.symptom: Cast-off edge is too tight and pulls the fabric in
items.cause: Casting off with the same tension as the body, which naturally tightens under the pass-over action
items.fix: Use a needle one or two sizes larger for the cast-off row, or consciously knit more loosely on the cast-off row before passing the stitches over.

items.symptom: Last stitch unravels after cutting the yarn
items.cause: Tail not pulled firmly through the last loop
items.fix: After drawing the tail through, pull firmly and then thread onto a darning needle to weave it in. The act of weaving in anchors the final stitch permanently.

items.symptom: Cast-off edge looks loopy and uneven
items.cause: Inconsistent tension when passing stitches over
items.fix: Give each passed-over stitch a small tug as it comes off the needle. Consistency matters more than tightness.
